title: The Loneliness of the Digital Nomad
coreMove: Treat freedom as shared availability, not private schedule control; a calendar becomes richer when it overlaps with the people, teams, rituals, and causes that give time its use.

exampleSpecs.stakes: The fantasy of outsourced chores may hide the loss of ordinary shared obligations.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Test the Super Mario fantasy against the shared rhythms that chores once created.

exampleSpecs.audience: a solo worker booking a long travel year
exampleSpecs.stakes: Spectacular places can feel hollow when nobody shares ordinary time around them.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Mark Manson's landmark travel to separate mobility from belonging.

exampleSpecs.stakes: Continuous coverage can look efficient while scattering families across different free days.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the Soviet continuous workweek to price the social cost of staggered rest days.

exampleSpecs.stakes: A blank weekday calendar can still feel poorer than a weekend because others are unavailable.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the weekend happiness rise as shared availability, not relief from employment.

exampleSpecs.audience: a laptop worker moving between cities
exampleSpecs.stakes: The digital nomad image can hide the ache of watching ordinary families from outside.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Mark Manson's lonely travel and the Japan park moment to test solitary mobility.

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer coordinator balancing flexible schedules
exampleSpecs.stakes: Total flexibility may preserve convenience while weakening the shared presence a campaign needs.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Contrast communal constraint with the scattered logic of staggered rest days.
